_meta.note: Named alternative SERVICE SHAPES for a Menaion feast, keyed M-D, opted into per parish via parish_settings.rubrics_extra_json {"menaionServiceSet": {"M-D": "<set>"}}. The same pattern as great-feast-variants.json antiphonSets: variable-sources/ text cannot use the overlay cascade, so a parish picks a named set instead of anyone editing the shared default. Name sets for their SOURCE and shape, never for a parish. Hymns are either a `ref` into the day's DB rows (by commemoration title fragment + section + order, or + type for troparia) or inline text stored in the Thee/Thy register.

raphaela-protection-daily._provenance: Daily Vespers of the Protection as sung from the Mother Raphaela Menaion (October 1 day-file, choir-site corpus) — Tyler 10.01.26 packet, docs/9-26 and 9-27 and 10.1/. Shared OCA rows are referenced; only the third Tone 4 sticheron, absent from the OCA text, is stored here.

menaion.label: (for the Protection)
menaion.text:
Thou art the beauty of Jacob
and the heavenly ladder upon which the Lord came down to earth.
These images were manifestations of thy honor and glory, Theotokos!
Angels in heaven and men on earth call thee blessed
for thou didst give birth to the God of all!
Thou prayest for all the world,//
by thy mercy, protecting those who keep thy holy feast!

oca-music-general-venerable-woman._provenance: Troparion only. The OCA publishes TWO troparia for Venerable Pelagia the Penitent and this set picks the second: oca.org/saints/troparia/<year>/10/08/ gives her PROPER troparion, Tone 4, "Like a fragrant rose growing among thorns" (our default, troparia.id=3355, source oca-menaion); the OCA Music Department's 2006 sheet instead sets the GENERAL troparion for a woman monastic, Tone 8. Both are OCA. St John of Damascus, Tyler sings the Music Department's — choir director, 2026-10-02 ("Use the general one…the image of God…"), and her sheet is docs/choir-packets/2026-10-01, daily-vespers-2026-10-08.pdf pp. 8-9. Text is our own algorithmic-yy2tt rendering of that troparion as it already renders for seven other venerable women (Apollinaria, Synkletika, …) with the name clause taken from her sheet. The dismissal Theotokion follows to Tone 8 on its own.

first.label: Venerable Pelagia the Penitent
first.text:
The image of God was truly preserved in thee, O Mother,
for thou didst take up thy cross and followed Christ.
By so doing, thou didst teach us to disregard the flesh, for it passes away;
but to care instead for the soul, since it is immortal.
Therefore, O venerable Pelagia, thy spirit rejoices with the Angels.
